extracted.intended_audience: hospital finance staff, GME/IME administrators, Medicare administrative contractors, hospital accountants, and other stakeholders preparing hospital cost reports and calculating Medicare DGME/IME payments (including during mergers and closures)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedures and standards for calculating direct GME (DGME) and indirect medical education (IME) payments when hospitals merge (including pre/post-merger partitioning, rolling averages, caps, PRA updates, patient loads, IRB ratio, and related reporting), and for redistribution of residency slots when teaching hospitals close.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre- and post-merger partitioning of cost reporting periods
rubrics_metrics.description: When a merger occurs during a cost reporting period, the MAC divides the cost reporting period into pre-merger and post-merger portions and calculates separate DGME and IME payments for each portion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat pre- and post-merger timeframes as though they were individual short cost reporting periods; compute payment variables separately for each and sum results to obtain total payment for the cost reporting period. If the surviving hospital begins a new cost reporting period effective with the date of the merger, use combined payment rates for that full new period.

rubrics_metrics.name: DGME FTE resident count computation
rubrics_metrics.description: Partial-year DGME FTE counts are determined by weighted FTE resident counts based on rotation schedules or similar documentation, following the methodology clarified in the August 4, 2025 Federal Register.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Calculate the sum of allowable rotations for all residents during the period, divide by the actual number of days in the period, and apply the DGME weighting methodology in the cited guidance. For pre-merger periods, include surviving provider rotations only; for post-merger periods, include combined rotations of merged providers.

rubrics_metrics.name: DGME FTE resident limit (cap) proration
rubrics_metrics.description: For DGME, the full-year DGME FTE cap must be prorated for partial (short) cost reporting periods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prorate the full-year DGME cap by multiplying by (days_in_period ÷ number_of_days_in_full_cost_year). Example: 40 × (123 ÷ 366) = prorated cap when the full cost reporting period includes Feb 29. The effective DGME resident count for the period is the lesser of the weighted DGME FTE count and the prorated cap.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three-year rolling average for DGME
rubrics_metrics.description: DGME payment uses a three-year rolling average of FTE counts (current, prior, penultimate years) adjusted for period lengths as needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prior- and penultimate-year FTE counts are divided by the number of days in those respective cost reporting periods and multiplied by the number of days in the partial (short) period being calculated, then averaged with the current period value: rolling_average = (current_period_adjusted + prior_adjusted + penultimate_adjusted) ÷ 3. For post-merger first two cost years, compute a 'virtual' rolling average by combining hospitals' prior and penultimate counts as if merged in those years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Per-resident amount (PRA) sourcing and update
rubrics_metrics.description: The PRA (single per resident amount) is sourced from the surviving hospital's most recently settled cost report and must be updated to the midpoint of the payment period using CPI-U inflation factors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the PRA from the most recently settled cost reporting period, then update it from that fiscal midpoint to the midpoint of the period for which payment is being calculated using an appropriate inflation factor estimating CPI‑U change (example multiplication factors shown in illustrations). The calculation of the inflation factor itself is done per the specified methodology (omitted in example).

rubrics_metrics.name: Medicare Part A and Medicare Advantage (MA) patient load calculations
rubrics_metrics.description: Medicare patient load is calculated as Medicare Part A inpatient days divided by total inpatient days; MA load is MA inpatient days divided by total inpatient days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a period spans calendar years, determine separate MA patient loads for the portions before and after January 1 because different percentage reductions to MA DGME/IME payments apply to different calendar years. Use combined inpatient days for merged hospitals when computing post-merger loads.

rubrics_metrics.name: MA DGME/IME payment reductions by calendar year
rubrics_metrics.description: MA DGME and MA IME payments are reduced by percentages determined by CMS for each calendar year and published in the Federal Register.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the year‑specific reduction factor to MA payments for the portion of the period falling in that calendar year. Example reductions used in illustrations: 2023 (2.74%), 2024 (2.33%).

rubrics_metrics.name: Merged PRA weighted averaging
rubrics_metrics.description: When hospitals merge, the merged PRA is computed as a weighted average of the individual hospitals' PRAs based on the number of DGME FTE residents reported on each hospital's most recently settled cost report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute merged PRA = ((FTE_A × PRA_A) + (FTE_B × PRA_B) + ...) ÷ total_FTEs_on_settled_reports, then update the merged PRA from the calendrical midpoint of the relevant fiscal year to the midpoint of the payment period using CPI-U inflation factors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Virtual merging for rolling averages in first two post-merger cost years
rubrics_metrics.description: For the first two cost reporting periods after a merger, compute the rolling average as though the hospitals had been merged during the entirety of their prior and penultimate cost reporting periods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine prior- and penultimate-year FTE counts of the surviving and terminating providers to form the numerator inputs to the three-year rolling average for the merged provider's first two post‑merger years. Standard rolling average computation resumes in the third full post‑merger cost reporting period.

rubrics_metrics.name: DGME reporting sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Inputs to DGME calculations (FTE counts, caps, PRA, inpatient days) come from hospitals' historical cost reports, rotation schedules, and PS&R reports, and PRAs are taken from most recently settled cost reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow instructions to lines of Worksheet E-4 and other cost report worksheets as referenced; use rotation schedules or similar documentation to determine resident rotations.

rubrics_metrics.name: IME FTE count computation
rubrics_metrics.description: Partial-year IME FTE counts are calculated by summing allowable rotations for residents during the pre- and post-merger periods and dividing by the actual number of days in each respective period, using master rotation schedules or similar sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For the pre-merger period include surviving provider rotations only; for post-merger include combined rotations of merged providers. Follow the FTE counting methodology clarified in the August 4, 2025 Federal Register.

rubrics_metrics.name: IME FTE cap (no proration for non-12-month periods)
rubrics_metrics.description: For IME, partial-year FTE resident limits are equal to the hospitals' original IME FTE caps (including adjustments) without proration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not prorate IME caps for non-12-month cost reporting periods; apply the original caps (pre-merger and combined post-merger) to the calculated IME FTE counts as usual.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three-year rolling average for IME
rubrics_metrics.description: The IME three-year rolling average uses current, prior, and penultimate-year IME counts (inputs from Worksheet E, Part A lines) without proration for short periods; post‑merger numerators simulate combined counts as if merged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obtain prior and penultimate counts from Worksheet E, Part A lines 13 and 14 of respective hospitals' cost reports (no proration). For post-merger calculations, combine the surviving and terminating providers' prior and penultimate counts to simulate merger effect for the rolling average during the first two post‑merger cost years.

rubrics_metrics.name: IRB ratio numerator: allowable IME FTE (subject to cap and rolling average)
rubrics_metrics.description: The IRB ratio numerator consists of the allowable IME FTE resident count, after application of the IME FTE cap and the three‑year rolling average.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine numerator separately for pre- and post-merger periods (pre-merger uses surviving provider only; post-merger uses combined providers). Include residents counted under special programs or displaced residents per Worksheet instructions where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Available bed count (IRB denominator) calculation
rubrics_metrics.description: The available bed count equals available bed days divided by the number of days in the virtual cost reporting period and is calculated separately for pre- and post-merger periods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For pre-merger, use surviving provider's available bed days in that period; for post-merger, include available bed days for all participating hospitals (including non-teaching hospitals). Compute bed days divided by days in period to get bed count.

rubrics_metrics.name: IRB ratio cap derivation and application
rubrics_metrics.description: The IRB ratio cap is derived from prior-year allowed IME FTE counts (Worksheet E, Part A, line 12) divided by prior-year available bed counts (Worksheet E, Part A, line 4), calculated separately for pre- and post-merger periods and without proration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pre-merger cap numerator/denominator use surviving provider prior year values; post-merger cap uses combined prior year values for all participating hospitals. Compute cap components without proration, compare the resulting IRB ratio to the cap, and use the lesser value in calculating teaching adjustment factors. Also compute a virtual IRB ratio cap for the first post-merger cost period simulating merger effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of lesser of IRB ratio and IRB ratio cap in teaching factor
rubrics_metrics.description: Compare the computed IRB ratio and the IRB ratio cap for the period and use the lesser of the two to calculate the IME teaching adjustment factor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply this comparison separately for pre- and post-merger periods; the resulting teaching adjustment factors are then multiplied by DRG revenue to obtain Part A and MA IME payments.

rubrics_metrics.name: DRG revenue accumulation and multiplication by teaching adjustment
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute Part A and simulated managed care DRG revenue for pre- and post-merger periods (from PS&R reports) and multiply by the corresponding teaching adjustment factors to obtain IME payments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pre-merger teaching adjustment factor multiplies surviving provider DRG revenue only; post-merger factor multiplies combined DRG revenue of participating hospitals. Simulated managed care revenue (shadow claims) is used for MA IME calculations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 422 resident treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: If providers count additional residents under section 422, those residents' payment calculations (IME) are performed separately with a special formula multiplier.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Calculate total IME payments for section 422 residents separately for pre- and post-merger periods, using the special formula multiplier of 0.66 for IME as applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Off-cost-report calculations for multiple payment rates
rubrics_metrics.description: Because the cost report does not support multiple IME (or DGME) payment rates within a single cost year, calculations for pre- and post-merger portions must be performed off the cost report and the results summed for reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute separate payment totals off the cost report and report the summed totals on the applicable lines of Worksheet E, Part A. Use placeholder values on cost report lines as necessary based on combined payment rates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjusting short-period prior-year FTE to 12-month equivalent
rubrics_metrics.description: When a hospital's prior cost reporting period was shorter than 12 months (e.g., terminating short period), inflate its prior‑year FTE count to a 12‑month equivalent for use in combined prior-year totals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Convert short-period FTE to 12-month equivalent by dividing the short-period FTE by the number of days in that period and multiplying by 365. Example: 16.55 ÷ 304 × 365 = 19.87 FTEs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sourcing prior-year worksheet data
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior- and penultimate-year FTE and bed counts used in rolling averages and IRB cap calculations are obtained from specific cost report lines (Worksheet E, Part A lines referenced).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use lines 12, 13, and 14 of Worksheet E, Part A for FTE counts and line 4 of Worksheet E, Part A for available beds. For non-teaching hospitals participating in the merger, determine bed count from Worksheet S-3, Part I (column 3, line 14 plus line 32) divided by number of days in prior year cost reporting period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Original PRA sourcing policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Individual hospitals' original (pre-merger) PRAs are sourced from the most recently settled cost reports, consistent with prior Federal Register policy (August 18, 2006).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the PRA reported on the most recently settled cost report as the starting point before applying inflation updates to the payment period midpoint.

rubrics_metrics.name: Residency slot redistribution after teaching hospital closure
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 5506 of the Affordable Care Act authorizes the Secretary to redistribute residency slots following closure of teaching hospitals and instructs CMS to establish a process and priority criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The regulation process (see 42 CFR 413.79(o)) redistributes slots to qualifying hospitals, with priority given to hospitals in the same Core Based Statistical Area (CBSA), a contiguous CBSA, or the same state as the closed hospital. CMS issues public notices initiating application rounds (example: Round 27 announced for Delaware County Memorial Hospital closure).
